reasoning: ROOT CAUSE: YAML aliases resolve to SHARED object references under yaml.safe_load (envh/core/config.py:140-144 _load_yaml). A preset doc with `env: &E {V0: &S AUTO_CANARY, V1..V2030: *S}` then `env: *E` on every other preset makes all 1548 presets share the SAME 2031-entry env dict (proven: id() identical across presets). parse_presets (config.py:307-314) loops over every preset and calls parse_preset, which (config.py:317-348) re-iterates raw_env.items() and runs VAR_NAME.match / SECRET_NAME.match / the known_secrets membership check PER VAR, PER PRESET -> O(presets x vars) ~= 3.14M validations on the shared node. This all runs on the broker's single asyncio event loop with NO await: control.py op_preset_validate (303-308) -> broker.validate_preset_yaml (broker.py:295-298) -> parse_presets, and the only await is the send() AFTER parsing, so the loop cannot service any other client or the console for the whole ~7s (concurrent rt1 status times out, reproduced). op_preset_propose (control.py:310-315) -> request_preset (broker.py:310-329) hits the same parse_presets during validation BEFORE _announce, so it wedges identically with no approval required to trigger it; op_import does not (JSON input, no aliases, plus the dump_presets size double-guard). refuse_oversized_presets (broker.py:66-70) checks only len(raw text) and the text is legitimately 62,805 B < 65,536. VERDICT: CONFIRMED HIGH. In scope (§3): socket-triggered event-loop wedge as non-root rt1, not a process kill, not OOM (peak RSS 0.38 GB under a serial flood), not root-flavored. Real impact (§4 DoS/INTEGRITY): a single unprivileged, unapproved, under-cap request deterministically freezes the entire broker AND the human console for ~7s (reproduced 4x at 7.2-7.4s), and the attack is trivially sustained to continuous total denial via concurrent connections well within MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_UID=32 (no approval, minimal audit trail) -> reliable DoS = HIGH. Novel (§5): a genuine bypass of V2's size cap and outside V1's error-path fix (see novelty). Skeptical notes: the ~7s per-request figure is CPU-dependent (a faster host sees a shorter single-request freeze), but (i) ~7s is near the ceiling achievable under the 64 KiB cap since presets x vars is maximized at this byte split, and (ii) the sustained multi-connection variant removes any CPU dependence and achieves full denial, so the HIGH rating does not rest on a single-request timing threshold.
recommended_fix: On the preset_validate/propose path, bound the EFFECTIVE parse work, not just raw bytes: cap total env-entries summed across all presets (e.g. refuse when sum(len(env)) exceeds a few thousand) and/or reject re-use of an aliased env node across presets (detect shared id()), or run parse_presets off the event loop in a worker with a time budget.
